authors: Aggarwal, Varinder K.; Lopin, Chrystel; Sandrinelli, Franck
citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2003), 125(25), 7596-7601
reference: New Insights in the Mechanism of Amine Catalyzed Epoxidation: Dual Role of Protonated Ammonium Salts as Both Phase Transfer Catalysts and Activators of Oxone | Aggarwal, Varinder K.; Lopin, Chrystel; Sandrinelli, Franck | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2003), 125(25), 7596-7601
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical experimental procedure for the epoxidation reactions described in Table 1, Table 3 and Scheme 10: The reaction was carried out in a flat bottomed glass vial (diameter 15mm) equipped with a magnetic stirrer flea. In the vial, were placed the amine 1 or the hydrochloride salt of amine 1, 2, 3, 7 or 8 (5 or 10 mol %, 0.0212 or 0.042 mmol), and 1-phenylcyclohexene (67 mg, 0.424 mmol). The mixture was dissolved in CH3CN/H2O (0.5 mL) and pyridine (0.5 eq., 0.212 mmol, 17 μL) was added followed by finely ground NaHCO3 (356 mg, 4.24 mmol) and Oxone® (521 mg, 0.848 mmol). The reaction was stirred at room temperature or at -10°C and followed by TLC. If the reaction was not complete, stirring was continued for a maximum of 2 hours. Salts were removed by filtration with a sinter over MgSO4. The cake was washed with CH2Cl2 (25 mL). When the reaction was performed at -10°C (Table 1, entries 4, 7 and 9), the organic phase was extracted with a saturated solution of NaHCO3 (to recover the amine). After evaporation of the dried organic phase, the crude mixture was analyzed by 1H NMR. Yields and conversions are determined by 1H NMR relative to an internal standard (para-dimethoxybenzene). The enantioselectivities were determined by chiral GC using a α-CD column. Procedure for reaction described in Scheme 5: The reaction has been performed following the procedure described above for Table 1 with CD3CN/D2O. After 5 min. of stirring at room temperature, the reaction mixture was diluted with CDCl3 (2 mL) in the presence of an internal standard. After 5 min. of stirring, the salts were allowed to settle. Solvent was decanted for NMR analysis. Yields are determined by 1H NMR relative to an internal standard (para-dimethoxybenzene). (S,S)-1-phenylcyclohexene oxide, yield 38%; potassium sulfate 6a, yield 90% 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3, 25 °C): = 1.20-1.71 (m, 4H; CH2), 1.92-2.38 (m, 4H; CH2), 3.01 (m, 1H; CHO), 7.21-7.53 (m, 5H; aromatic H). The absolute configuration was determined by comparing the measured optical rotation with the reported one: [α]D20 = -54.8 (c = 0.47 in toluene) [lit.[5] for the (R,R)-1-phenylcyclohex-1-ene oxide: [α]D25 = +116.7 (c = 1.21 in benzene) for 98% ee].

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: (Table 2, entry 1) erythro-1-(2-Ethyl-oxiranyl)-propan-1-ol. General Procedure C: Epoxidation with Ti(OiPr)4 and Dioxygen. A 10 mL Schlenk flask was charged with (-)-MIB (5.0 mg, 0.020 mmol) and 1 mL hexanes and cooled to 0 °C. A hexanes solution of Et2Zn (0.5 mL, 2.0 M) was added, followed by addition of 2-ethylpropenal (52 μL, 0.5 mmol) dropwise. The reaction was stirred at 0 °C for 8 h until alkyl addition was complete by TLC. The reaction flask was then capped with a balloon of oxygen. After stirring at 0 °C for 1 h, the reaction flask was cooled to -20 °C, and a hexanes solution of Ti(OiPr)4 (0.05 mL, 1.0 M) was added. The reaction continued to stir at -20 °C under an O2 atmosphere for 18 h. It was then quenched with 15% tartaric acid solution, allowed to stir for 45 min, and poured into a separatory funnel with a solution of Na2S2O4. The organic and aqueous layers were separated, and the aqueous layer was extracted with hexanes (3 X 10 mL). The combined organic layers were then washed with brine and H2O and dried over MgSO4. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 3.7 mmol triphenylmethyl substituted olefin, 0.042 g salen Mn (III) (about 15 mol%) and 5 mL CH2Cl2 were added into a 100 mL three-neck flask. At 0 °C 20 mL of a solution of DMD in acetone (0.1 mol·L-1) was rapidly dropwise added. Upon addition, the reaction mixture was warmed slowly to room temperature and further violently stirred. The reaction process was traced by TLC. After 24 h, additional 20 mL solution of DMD in acetone (approx. 0.1 mol·L-1) was dropwise added over 2 h by controlling the dropping rate. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure D: Epoxidation with Ti(OiPr)4 and TBHP. A 10 mL Schlenk flask was charged with (-)-MIB (4.8 mg, 0.020 mmol) and 2 mL of hexanes and cooled to 0 °C. A hexanes solution of Et2Zn (0.75 mL, 2.0 M) was added, followed by addition of 2-ethylpropenal (49 μL, 0.5 mmol) dropwise. The reaction was stirred at 0 °C for 20 h until alkyl addition was complete by TLC, then the reaction flask was cooled to -20 °C. A solution of Ti(OiPr)4 in dichloromethane (100 μL, 1.0 M) was added, followed by dropwise, careful addition of a decane solution of TBHP (0.45 mL, 5.5 M). The reaction continued to stir at -20 °C for 8 h. It was then quenched with 4 mL saturated aq NH4Cl, allowed to stir for 30 min at room temp, and poured into a separatory funnel with a solution of Na2S2O4. The organic and aqueous layers were separated, and the aqueous layer was extracted with diethyl ether (3 X 5 mL). The combined organic layers were then washed with 5 mL brine and 5 mL H2O and dried over MgSO4. The filtrate was concentrated in vacuo, and the residue was chromatographed on silica (10% ethyl acetate in hexanes) to afford the title compound as a colorless oil in 65% yield (42 mg, 0.32 mmol).

experimental_procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. Epoxidation of the Enecarbamate Z-1a by DMD According to the general procedure GP1, 397.5 mg (1.96 mmol) of enecarbamate Z-1a were epoxidized with DMD during 1 h. After work-up, the racemic epoxide (1S*,2S*)-2a was obtained as colorless oil in 94% yield (403.8 mg). The material decomposed at ca. 20 °C within a couple of hours, such that an exact-mass determination was not possible. Characterisation rests only on the NMR-spectral data. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: (Table 2, entry 1) erythro-1-(2-Ethyl-oxiranyl)-propan-1-ol. General Procedure C: Epoxidation with Ti(OiPr)4 and Dioxygen. A 10 mL Schlenk flask was charged with (-)-MIB (5.0 mg, 0.020 mmol) and 1 mL hexanes and cooled to 0 °C. A hexanes solution of Et2Zn (0.5 mL, 2.0 M) was added, followed by addition of 2-ethylpropenal (52 μL, 0.5 mmol) dropwise. The reaction was stirred at 0 °C for 8 h until alkyl addition was complete by TLC. The reaction flask was then capped with a balloon of oxygen. After stirring at 0 °C for 1 h, the reaction flask was cooled to -20 °C, and a hexanes solution of Ti(OiPr)4 (0.05 mL, 1.0 M) was added. The reaction continued to stir at -20 °C under an O2 atmosphere for 18 h. It was then quenched with 15% tartaric acid solution, allowed to stir for 45 min, and poured into a separatory funnel with a solution of Na2S2O4. The organic and aqueous layers were separated, and the aqueous layer was extracted with hexanes (3 X 10 mL). The combined organic layers were then washed with brine and H2O and dried over MgSO4. The filtrate was concentrated in vacuo, and the residue was chromatographed on silica (20% ethyl acetate in hexanes) to afford the title compound as a colorless oil in 60% yield (39 mg, 0.30 mmol).

Styrene was selected as model substrate and treated with Fe3O4/SiO2 NPs in the presence of m-CPBA as the oxygen donor at room temperature under different conditions. This reaction was best carried out using 2 equiv. of m-CPBA for 4 h at room temperature in dichloromethane. The catalytic activity of the Fe3O4NPs was also investigated in the epoxidation of styrene, and low yield (45 %) was observed. reference: Bifunctional Nanocrystalline MgO for Chiral Epoxy Ketones via Claisen-Schmidt Condensation-Asymmetric Epoxidation Reactions | Choudary, Boyapati M.; Kantam, Mannepalli L.; Ranganath, Kalluri V. S.; Mahendar, Koosam; Sreedhar, Bojja | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2004), 126(11), 3396-3397
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the preparation of chiral epoxide: Chalcone (0.500 g, 2.5 mmol), TBHP (3.7 M in toluene, 4.0 mL, 15mmol), NAP-MgO (0.200 g), and (+)-diethyl tartrate (0.047l g, 0.275 mmol) were placed under nitrogen atmosphere in a dry 50 mL flask containing 15 mL of dry toluene (additional 1 mL of THF for substituted chalcones) and stirred at 25 ºC for 36 h. After completion of the reaction (monitored by TLC), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to separate the catalyst and washed with ether. The filtrate was quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl (10 mL), and 10% aqueous Na2SO3 (15 mL) and diethyl ether (10 mL) was added. The aqueous layer was washed with diethyl ether (3x10 mL), and the combined organic extracts were washed with saturated aqueous NaCl, dried over MgSO4, and the solvent was removed under reduced pressure. After purification by flash chromatography on silica gel using 20% ethyl acetate in petroleum ether. α,β-epoxy ketone was obtained. (+)-Diethyl tartrate can be recovered quantitatively with no observable change in enantiomeric purity from the same chromatographic column by increasing the proportion of ethyl acetate in the eluent. trans-(2R,3S)-Epoxy-1, 3-diphenylpropan-1-one. authors: Nam, Wonwoo; Lim, Mi Hee; Lee, Ha Jin; Kim, Cheal
citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2000), 122(28), 6641-6647
reference: Evidence for the Participation of Two Distinct Reactive Intermediates in Iron(III) Porphyrin Complex-Catalyzed Epoxidation Reactions | Nam, Wonwoo; Lim, Mi Hee; Lee, Ha Jin; Kim, Cheal | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2000), 122(28), 6641-6647
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Catalytic Competitive Epoxidations in Protic and Aprotic Solvents. Reactions were performed at ambient temperature under argon atmosphere unless otherwise indicated. All reactions were run in at least triplicate, and the data reported represent the average of these reactions. The competitive epoxidations of cis- and trans-stilbenes and of cyclooctene and trans-stilbene in protic solvent were carried out as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3OH/CH2Cl2 (3:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (0.15 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3OH and CH2Cl2 (3:1). The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC. Product yields were determined by comparison against standard curves. The reaction conditions in aprotic solvent were as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3CN/CH2Cl2 (1:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (1.0 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3CN and CH2Cl2 (1:1). The competitive epoxidations studied with H2O2 were carried out in the presence of 5-chloro-1-methylimidazole (0.1 mmol), since the epoxidation of olefins by iron porphyrin complexes and H2O2 in aprotic solvent did not yield epoxide products in the absence of the imidazole.23 The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC with known authentic samples. Cyclooctene oxide, yield 10%; trans-stilbene oxide, yield 87%.

experimental_procedure: 8β-tert-Butyldimethylsilyloxy-des-A,B-9α,11α-epoxyandros tane (11). 3-Chloroperoxybenzoic acid (4.87 g, 27.7 mmol) was added in portions to a stirred solution of 10 (2.61 g, 9.81 mmol) in dry CH2Cl2 (100 mL) at 0 °C. The mixture was stirred in the dark for 2 h at 0 °C and for 3 h at room temperature. The reaction was quenched by the addition of Na2S2O4 (80 mL, saturated aqueous solution). The resulting mixture was vigorously shaken and the aqueous layer was extracted with CH2Cl2 (3 x 50 mL). The combined organic solution was dried, filtered, and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by flash chromatography on silica gel (3% Et2O/hexanes) to afford 11 [2.58 g, 9.12 mmol, 93%, Rf = 0.3 (hexanes), colorless oil]. 8β-tert-Butyldimethylsilyloxy-des-A,B-9a, 11a-epoxyandrostane (11). 1H-NMR (CDC13, 250 MHz, δ): 4.20 (1H, broad d, J = 1.8 Hz, H-8), 3.17 (1H, dd, J= 5.8 and 3.5 Hz, H-l l), 3.09 (1H, m, H-9), 0.92 (9H, s, t BuSi), 0.89 (3H, s, Me-18), 0.11 (3H, s, MeSi), 0.06 (3H, s, MeSi). 13C-NMR (CDC13, 62.89 MHz, δ): 66.92 (CH), 56.83 (CH), 52.78 (CH), 43.49 (CH), 40.47 (CH2), 39.04 (CH2), 38.25 (C), 25.77 (CH3), 22.49 (CH3), 22.44 (CH2), 20.16 (CH2), 17.99 (C), -4.71 (CH3), -5.20 (CH3). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Catalytic Olefin Epoxidations by Cobalt Catalyst with MCPBA. To a mixture of substrate (0.035 mmol), cobalt catalyst (0.001 mmol), and solvent (CH3CN, 1 mL) was added MCPBA (0.05 mmol). The mixture was stirred for 10 min at room temperature, even though the reaction was complete within 1 min at room temperature (Figure S1). Reaction was monitored by GC/mass analysis of 20 μL aliquots withdrawn periodically from the reaction mixture. All reactions were run at least three times, and the average product yields are presented. Product yields were based on substrate. In a competitive reaction of cis-2-octene and trans-2-octene, the concentration of the substrate was 0.20 mmol, respectively. Yield (97.9 ± 1.7%).

experimental_procedure: Catalytic Competitive Epoxidations in Protic and Aprotic Solvents. Reactions were performed at ambient temperature under argon atmosphere unless otherwise indicated. All reactions were run in at least triplicate, and the data reported represent the average of these reactions. The competitive epoxidations of cis- and trans-stilbenes and of cyclooctene and trans-stilbene in protic solvent were carried out as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3OH/CH2Cl2 (3:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (0.15 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3OH and CH2Cl2 (3:1). The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC. Product yields were determined by comparison against standard curves. The reaction conditions in aprotic solvent were as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3CN/CH2Cl2 (1:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (1.0 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3CN and CH2Cl2 (1:1). The competitive epoxidations studied with H2O2 were carried out in the presence of 5-chloro-1-methylimidazole (0.1 mmol), since the epoxidation of olefins by iron porphyrin complexes and H2O2 in aprotic solvent did not yield epoxide products in the absence of the imidazole.23 The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC with known authentic samples. cis-stilbene oxide, yield 88%; trans-stilbene oxide, yield 11%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: (Table 2, entry 9) erythro-1-(7-Oxa-bicyclo[4.1.0]hept-1-yl)-ethanol. General Procedure E: Epoxidation with Ti(OtBu)4 and Dioxygen. A 10 mL Schlenk flask was charged with bis(sulfonamide) ligand L* 2 (3.8 mg, 0.01 mmol), Ti(OtBu)4 (97 μL, 0.25 mmol), and 0.5 mL hexanes and stirred for 30 min at room temp. A hexanes solution of Me2Zn (0.25 mL, 0.50 mmol) was then added, and after stirring for 10 min, cyclohexenecarboxaldehyde (14 μL, 0.13 mmol) was added. The reaction was stirred at room temp for 20 h, until alkyl addition was complete by TLC, then cooled to 0 °C. 1 equiv Me2Zn (63μL, 0.13 mmol) was added; the reaction flask was capped with a balloon of oxygen, warmed to room temperature and allowed to stir under an O2 atmosphere for 19 h. It was then quenched with 15% tartaric acid solution, allowed to stir for 45 min, poured into a separatory funnel with a solution of Na2S2O4. The organic and aqueous layers were separated, and the aqueous layer was extracted with hexanes (3 X 10 mL). The combined organic layers were then washed with brine and H2O and dried over MgSO4. The filtrate was concentrated in vacuo, and the residue was chromatographed on silica (10% ethyl acetate in hexanes) to afford the title compound as a colorless oil in 78% yield (14 mg, 0.099 mmol).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure. To the solution of complex Mn-2 (1.0 μmol, 0.68 mg) in CH3CN (0.4 mL) (or methanol, 0.5 mL), thermostated at desired temperature, the substrate (200 μmol) was added in one portion, and 250 μmol of AcOOH (or 250 μmol of HCO3H) was slowly added within 3 min. The mixture was stirred for a desired period of time (10 min up to 3h). Then 1.5 mL of saturated aqueous NaHCO3 was added and the aqueous phase was extracted with pentane (3×2 mL). The solvent was carefully removed in a stream of air, the residue was dissolved in 1.0 mL CCl4 and dried over CaSO4. The mixture was filtered and the filtrate analyzed by 1H NMR spectroscopy. The yield was calculated based on the portion of the epoxide in the reaction mixture (for examples see Figure S1). The concentrations of the products in reaction mixtures were established based on comparison with the solutions of the starting olefin of known concentration in the same solvent (CCl4 ). The admixture of trichloroethylene (δ 6.46) in CCl4 served as a side reference for peaks integration. A similar procedure was applied for catalysts Mn-3 and Mn-4. The enantiomeric excess values were analyzed either by 1H NMR with a chiral shift reagent Eu(hfc)3(for the epoxides of styrene, trans-β-methylstyrene, 1,2-dihydronaphthalene, indene, 1-octene) or by chiral HPLC (styrene epoxide, dbpcn epoxide). If organic hydroperoxides, m-CPBA or iodosylarenes were used as oxidants, the catalyst:substrate:oxidant ratio was 1:100:110. Entry no. 6; T, -20 °C; time, 2 h; conversion, 97.5 %.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: (Table 2, entry 1) erythro-1-(2-Ethyl-oxiranyl)-propan-1-ol. General Procedure C: Epoxidation with Ti(OiPr)4 and Dioxygen. A 10 mL Schlenk flask was charged with (-)-MIB (5.0 mg, 0.020 mmol) and 1 mL hexanes and cooled to 0 °C. A hexanes solution of Et2Zn (0.5 mL, 2.0 M) was added, followed by addition of 2-ethylpropenal (52 μL, 0.5 mmol) dropwise. The reaction was stirred at 0 °C for 8 h until alkyl addition was complete by TLC. The reaction flask was then capped with a balloon of oxygen. After stirring at 0 °C for 1 h, the reaction flask was cooled to -20 °C, and a hexanes solution of Ti(OiPr)4 (0.05 mL, 1.0 M) was added. The reaction continued to stir at -20 °C under an O2 atmosphere for 18 h. It was then quenched with 15% tartaric acid solution, allowed to stir for 45 min, and poured into a separatory funnel with a solution of Na2S2O4. The organic and aqueous layers were separated, and the aqueous layer was extracted with hexanes (3 X 10 mL). The combined organic layers were then washed with brine and H2O and dried over MgSO4. The filtrate was concentrated in vacuo, and the residue was chromatographed on silica (20% ethyl acetate in hexanes) to afford the title compound as a colorless oil in 60% yield (39 mg, 0.30 mmol).
notes: stereoselective, enantioselective

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. Epoxidation of the Enecarbamate Z-1a by DMD According to the general procedure GP1, 397.5 mg (1.96 mmol) of enecarbamate Z-1a were epoxidized with DMD during 1 h. After work-up, the racemic epoxide (1S*,2S*)-2a was obtained as colorless oil in 94% yield (403.8 mg). The material decomposed at ca. 20 °C within a couple of hours, such that an exact-mass determination was not possible. Characterisation rests only on the NMR-spectral data. Epoxidation of the Enecarbamate Z-1c by DMD According to the general procedure GP1, 619.8 mg (2.22 mmol) of the enecarbamate Z-1c were epoxidized with DMD for 4 h. After work-up, a diastereomeric mixture (92:8) of the epoxides (1R,2R)-2c and (1S,2S)-2c was obtained as colorless oil in ca. 100% yield (655.1 mg). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: 3.7 mmol triphenylmethyl substituted olefin, 0.042 g salen Mn (III) (about 15 mol%) and 5 mL CH2Cl2 were added into a 100 mL three-neck flask. At 0 °C 20 mL of a solution of DMD in acetone (0.1 mol·L-1) was rapidly dropwise added. Upon addition, the reaction mixture was warmed slowly to room temperature and further violently stirred. The reaction process was traced by TLC. After 24 h, additional 20 mL solution of DMD in acetone (approx. 0.1 mol·L-1) was dropwise added over 2 h by controlling the dropping rate. After that, the reaction was further violently stirred at room temperature for 20 h. Upon completion, the solvent was removed under reduced pressure, and the residue purified by chromatography on silica gel column [developing agent: mixture solvent of petroleum ether and ethyl ether (10 : 1, V : V)] to give a yellowish solid. The resulting solid was recrystallized from a little n-hexane to afford a white or colorless crystal. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Catalytic Competitive Epoxidations in Protic and Aprotic Solvents. Reactions were performed at ambient temperature under argon atmosphere unless otherwise indicated. All reactions were run in at least triplicate, and the data reported represent the average of these reactions. The competitive epoxidations of cis- and trans-stilbenes and of cyclooctene and trans-stilbene in protic solvent were carried out as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3OH/CH2Cl2 (3:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (0.15 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3OH and CH2Cl2 (3:1). The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC. Product yields were determined by comparison against standard curves. The reaction conditions in aprotic solvent were as follows: oxidants (0.05 mmol, diluted in 0.3 mL of CH3CN/CH2Cl2 (1:1)) were slowly added over a period of 20 min to a stirred solution containing an iron porphyrin complex (1 x 10-3 mmol) and equal amounts of competing olefins (1.0 mmol each) in a solvent mixture (2.2 mL) of CH3CN and CH2Cl2 (1:1). The competitive epoxidations studied with H2O2 were carried out in the presence of 5-chloro-1-methylimidazole (0.1 mmol), since the epoxidation of olefins by iron porphyrin complexes and H2O2 in aprotic solvent did not yield epoxide products in the absence of the imidazole.23 The reaction mixture was further stirred for 10 min and directly analyzed by HPLC and/or GC with known authentic samples. Cyclooctene oxide, yield 93%; trans-stilbene oxide.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure D: Epoxidation with Ti(OiPr)4 and TBHP. A hexanes solution of Et2Zn (0.75 mL, 2.0 M) was added, followed by addition of 2-ethylpropenal (49 μL, 0.5 mmol) dropwise. The combined organic layers were then washed with 5 mL brine and 5 mL H2O and dried over MgSO4. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Epoxidation of the Enecarbamates 1 with Dimethyldioxirane (GP1) The enecarbamate 1 (1.0 equiv.) was dissolved in acetone (30 mL) and 0.50 g of molecular sieves (5 Å) was added under an argon-gas atmosphere. The solution was cooled to 0 °C and after 10 min magnetic stirring, 1.0 equiv. of dimethyldioxirane (0.09 M in acetone) was added. The reaction mixture was allowed to warm up to ca. 20 °C while stirring, and the reaction progress was monitored for the presence of DMD by iodometry (KI/HOAC). After complete DMD consumption (the reaction times are given for the individual cases), the reaction mixture was centrifuged to remove the molecular sieves, the sieves were washed with acetone (2x15 mL) and centrifuged again. From the combined centrifugates, the acetone was removed (20 °C, 30 mbar) and the epoxide 2 was obtained as only product. The epoxides 2 were too labile for purification by silica-gel chromatography, and were characterized by their 1H-and 13C-NMR spectra and exact mass determination on the diastereomeric mixture [except epoxide 2a, which decomposed completely already at room temperature (ca. 20 °C) in a couple of hours]. The diastereomeric ratio was determined by 1H-NMR analysis directly on the crude reaction mixture, through integration of the areas under the characteristic NMR signals. In the case of nearly 1:1 mixtures of the diastereomers, COSY, HMBC and HMQC experiments were carried out for rigorous assignment. For the configurational assignment of the individual diastereomers, see General Procedure GP3. The epoxides 2b-d persist as neat solids for several months at -20 °C, but they readily decompose in solution in the presence of acid traces at room temperature (ca. 20 °C). For this reason, after formation, the labile epoxides must be immediately worked up to remove the solvent and the molecular sieves to minimize decomposition. Epoxidation of the Enecarbamate Z-1a by DMD According to the general procedure GP1, 397.5 mg (1.96 mmol) of enecarbamate Z-1a were epoxidized with DMD during 1 h. After work-up, the racemic epoxide (1S*,2S*)-2a was obtained as colorless oil in 94% yield (403.8 mg). The material decomposed at ca. 20 °C within a couple of hours, such that an exact-mass determination was not possible. Characterisation rests only on the NMR-spectral data. Epoxidation of the Enecarbamate Z-1d by DMD According with the general procedure GP1, 556.8 mg (2.15 mmol) of the enecarbamate Z-1d were epoxidized with DMD for 4 h. After work-up, a diastereomeric mixture (93:7) of the epoxides (1R,2R)-2d and (1S,2S)-2d was obtained as a colorless powder in 95% yield (561.7 mg).
